42:- P-44 **`AnyIntegral`'s closure stands, and the checker reads `comprises` the 2012 way.** The closure `AnyIntegral comprises { ... }` stands, with a `NOT YET` comment in the team's wording. So do the generic scalar-extension block, the `AnyAdditiveGroup` marker and the `Array3` exclusion. A generic child of a closed trait may extend it when every type that the checker knows below it is listed. The clause's text and walk stay as they are. Row 487 records the hole that every reading but the 2008 one shares: a program's own `Integral` subtype in another component is not caught.
60:- P-146 **The checker reads `self` in a self-typed trait's method bodies as the implementing type (way 6).** In a trait `C[\X\]` whose parameter `X` extends `C[\X\]`, `self` in the trait's method bodies has the type `C[\X\] & X`; the signatures keep the plain trait type, as the POPL 2019 paper's assumption on declared types needs. A type that extends such a trait at another type is refused, Scala's conformance rule. The library's text gains no self type and no `comprises` clause, and walk is unchanged. It clears 29 sites of the distance; the thirtieth takes one `numerator` per integer type. Why: it reads the library as the team wrote it, as P-44 does, by one rule the peers share. Built by climb batch 14 (`1c32ccffd`).
- F-220 **`__bigOperator`'s local `body` is typed `body(i: I): L`, which walk runs since it no longer instantiates a big operator's static parameter at `BottomType`.** The checker count passes it (F-53). Gated by `tests/UnwrittenListMapComprehensionWalk`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-elements/REPORT.md` section 6.
- F-221 **The compiled checker retries a call written as another call's argument against each enclosing declaration's parameter type, where the enclosing call is not accepted otherwise.** It builds P-51 under P-49, so a declaration that accepts the call as written is never passed over. A reduction's plain-bounded big operator, an argument of `__bigOperator` once desugared, so takes the reduction's expected type; an F-bounded one is still refused (row 731). A chain `a OPLUS b OPLUS c` that only the retry makes acceptable to a multifix declaration now runs it, not the binary one. Walk gives such an argument no expected type (row 705). Gated by `compiler_tests/InferCallArgument*` and `InferBigOperatorExpectedType`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-argument-context/REPORT.md` sections 1, 5 and 8, and `SKEPTIC.md` finding 5.
- F-225 **The compiled checker types `self` in a self-typed trait's method bodies as the implementing type, read from the trait's F-bound, keeps the signatures plain, and refuses an extender at another type.** It builds P-146. The library's 29 self-typed bodies check. Walk loads what the rule refuses. A compiled body that returns `self` fails verification when the parameter is an object type (row 695). The rule refuses the team demo `trips.fss`'s `generator` (row 710) and `PureList`'s `List` (row 355). Gated by `compiler_tests/SelfType*` and `XXXSelfType*`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-self-type/REPORT.md` sections 1, 2, 4 and 7.
- F-226 **The compiled checker renames an inherited method's own static parameters apart before it uses them: from its trait's in the overloading check, and from the receiver's static arguments at a call.** So `Generator.generate[\R\]`, inherited by `PossibleReductionPair[\R\]`, keeps its own `R` (row 561). At a call, each method that `commonInheritedMethods` returns is instantiated with those of its own static parameters whose names the arguments mention renamed to `name$i`, so a method invocation and a call by name inside a trait are repaired alike. Gated by `compiler_tests/InheritedMethodStaticParamSameName`, `InheritedMethodByNameStaticParamSameName` and `MethodStaticArgReceiverSameName`. Detail: `perf-probes/nat/triage.md` section 3; `compile-ladder/rung-checker-contexts/REPORT.md` section 1.
- F-227 **The compiled checker keeps an intersection that names a type or inference variable as written, and reads a variable below a union through the union whole or its bound.** A closed trait is expanded into its listed types only against a conjunct that names no variable (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:708-735`, `:165-180`). So a call through a parameter bounded by a closed trait and a bound excluding a listed type checks, and the Return Type Rule beside it (rows 686, 687, 689, 690 and 711). A `Box[\T\]` argument under a ground second bound stays refused (row 712), and an overloading the base accepted through the expansion is refused (row 713). Gated by `compiler_tests/*TwoBoundsClosedTrait` and `*TwoGroundBounds*ClosedTrait`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-checker-bounds/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 6.

# Decision record: the type of `self` in a trait with a self-type parameter (rung S, climb batch 14)

This is the decision record the S1 form asks for (POSITIONS, "The S1 form"; the `fortress-repo` skill's `references/specification.md`, "Changing the text: the revision form", part 4): each changed passage, the original and the new text, the reason, and the way back. Appendix I's entry "The type of `self` in a trait with a self-type parameter" (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:3296-3412`, `\seclabel{revival-self-type}`) names this file. The base is `5bf8a7c84`. "The Working Draft of February 2011" is the unrevised copy under `Specification-1.0-frozen/`.

The decision this rung carries out is P-146, "The checker reads `self` in a self-typed trait's method bodies as the implementing type (way 6)", from the judgement's recommendation (`explorations/reviews/self-typed-bodies-judgement.md`, section 4), with the default the coordinator took under it after the batch record's review and listed for review (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-14.md:86`): a trait's type parameter bounded by a self-typed trait that the trait extends at that parameter counts as the trait's self parameter too, never an object's. The form follows P-95 and P-96.

## 1. A word, before the passages

The specification already says "self parameter" for the parameter named `self` of a method (`Specification/basic/overloading.tex:167-182`, `Specification/basic/traits.tex:577`, `:591`, `:631`, `:644`, `Specification/preliminaries/overview.tex:1140-1146`). The checker's code and the record call the trait's static parameter that `self` is read as "the self parameter" (`SelfParamDisambiguator.selfParam`; the judgement, way 6). So the text calls the static parameter a **self-type parameter**, and keeps "self parameter" for `self`. The checker's message keeps the record's wording, "whose self parameter is A" (the batch record, section S, "Rule (b), not yet built"), which reads as the instantiation's argument for the trait's static self parameter.

## 2. The passages

### 2.1 The type of `self` (`Specification/basic/expressions/var-ref.tex`, section "Identifier References")

- Original: `Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/var-ref.tex:53-54` and `:64-69`, the same text as the base's `var-ref.tex:53-54`, `:64-69`, unchanged by this rung: "The type of `self` is the type of the trait or object being declared by the innermost enclosing trait or object declaration or object expression." and the self-type idiom, "If the innermost enclosing such construct is a trait declaration (for a trait called, say, `T`), and that trait declaration has a `comprises` clause, and `U_1`, `U_2`, ..., `U_n` are the traits mentioned in the `comprises` clause, then the type of `self` is instead `T ∩ (U_1 ∪ U_2 ∪ ... ∪ U_n)`."
- New text, `var-ref.tex:70-79`, after the idiom's sentence: "If that trait declaration has no `comprises` clause, or one that lists no type but `...`, and has a self-type parameter `X` (§ trait-decls), a static parameter bounded by the trait itself at its own static parameters, as in `trait T[\X extends T[\X\]\]`, or by a trait with a self-type parameter that `T` extends at `X`, then the type of `self` in the bodies of its methods is instead `T ∩ X`; the `self` parameter keeps the type `T` in the signature of each method declaration, which overloading and the choice of a declaration at a call read." The callout follows at `:80-90`.
- Reason. Rule (a) of way 6 (the judgement, section 3, "Way 6"): a bound constrains the argument, not `self`; a body that treats `self` as the parameter is sound only under a further fact, which Scala gets from a declared self type checked at each extender. The checker's own self type under a `comprises` clause (`SelfParamDisambiguator.scala:56-75`, `TypeAnalyzer.removeSelf`), which the team pinned in `XXX10k.test`, is read from the bound that the library already writes. Naden asked for exactly this, "a separate construct which cannot be used as a first class type, but instead only in bounds" (`Papers/Types/journal/justificationOfRTR.tex:626-630`).
- The confinement's reason, the signatures kept at the trait's type. The POPL 2019 paper (Park, Hong, Steele and Ryu) has no self types, so it neither supports nor contradicts rules (a) and (b); but its matching of types is complete only for types that hold no type parameter inside a union or intersection, an assumption it shows every declared type meets (pp. 11:21-22, `research/extracts/ParkPOPL2019-extract.md:258-264`), and its Return Type Rule compares declared domains (p. 11:13). The unconfined rule put `C[\X\] & X` into the functional methods' signatures and the distance stage then reported 18 Return Type Rule errors between `StandardPartialOrder`'s and `StandardTotalOrder`'s `CMP`, whose domains became equivalent, and 3 call sites typed `Comparison` (the judgement, "Rule (a) alone, as section 6 asks"; `explorations/reviews/array-judgements-popl-check.md`, section 5). Keeping the se

### 2.2 Self-type parameters and their extenders (`Specification/basic/traits.tex`, section "Trait Declarations")

- Original: none; the paragraph is new, at `traits.tex:285-326`, after the `comprises` passage and its note on `...` (`:235-283`) and before the `Catalyst` example.
- New text: a trait with no `comprises` clause, or one that lists no type but `...`, may have a self-type parameter, a static parameter `X` whose bounds include the trait at its own static parameters, or an instantiation of a trait with a self-type parameter that the trait also lists in its `extends` clause, with `X` as the static argument for that self-type parameter; `self` then has the type `T ∩ X` in its methods' bodies; a trait or object declaration, or an object expression, that extends an instantiation of `T` must be a subtype of the static argument for the self-type parameter, a trait standing as the type of `self` in its bodies, the intersection of its type with the types its `comprises` clause lists or with its own self-type parameter `Y`; an object declaration has none. The example, `trait Shape[\S extends Shape[\S\]\] end`, `object Point extends Shape[\Point\] end`, and `ob
- Reason. Rule (b) of way 6: Scala's conformance rule, "The self type of a class or object must conform to the self types of all classes which are inherited by the template" (*Scala Language Specification 2.13*, section 5.1, as `explorations/reviews/self-typed-bodies-ways.md:304` cites it). Checking direct extensions at every declaration suffices, by induction up the hierarchy: a value of `C[\A\]` comes from an object whose every supertrait was checked (the judgement, way 6, (b)). The widened reading (the coordinator's default) keeps the team's 2009 mixins `ContainmentBySubset[\T extends Containment[\T\]\] extends Containment[\T\]` and `ContainmentByComparison` (`Library/Containment.fsi:22-30`, `.fss:42`, `:57`) valid as written, rule (b) then checking their extenders, `Relation` among them (`Library/Relation.fsi:17`, `.fss:23`). An object has no self-type parameter, so `object M[\T exte

### 2.3 The type of a functional method's `self` parameter (`Specification/basic/traits.tex`, section "Method Declarations")

- Original: `Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/traits.tex:486`, unchanged at `traits.tex:598`: "This parameter is not given a type and implicitly has the type of the enclosing trait or object."
- New text: a callout at `traits.tex:599-603`: under a self-type parameter the sentence still holds of the declaration's signature, and in the body `self` has the type `T ∩ X`. The sentence stays true under the confinement, so it is not revised; the callout says so. `Specification/basic/overloading.tex:180-182`, "Note that the static type of the self parameter is the trait or object trait type in which the declaration occurs", stays true for the same reason and gets no callout.

### 2.4 Appendix I

One entry before "Passages not yet revised", `changes.tex:3296-3412`: affected sections, change, rationale (P-146 by its date, 13 October 2026, and the default by its date, 14 October 2026; the library's 29 bodies; Scala's rule; the team's `XXX10k`; Naden; the 2019 paper's reason for the confinement), effect (the checker; walk unchanged and loading what the rule refuses; the code generator's `VerifyError`, row 695), the original text of `var-ref.tex` quoted and `traits.tex:486` named, and route C.

The calculi of Appendix A are untouched, with no new callout: they type `self` as the trait and admit no self type, which their existing callouts already say they predate (the judgement, section 5, "Specification").

## 3. The way back

- To P-146's letter, without the default: the widened reading goes (the second form of a self-type parameter, in `SelfParamDisambiguator.throughBound` and its environment, and the text's "or by a trait with a self-type parameter that `T` extends at `X`"), and rule (b) then refuses the two `Containment` mixins' extension of `Containment[\T\]` until their text changes. `SelfTypeMixinBound` turns red, `XXXSelfTypeMixinExtenderWrong` red ("Saw wrong failure").
- To the Working Draft: rule (a), the confinement and rule (b) go; the 29 library bodies are refused again by the checker (the distance's S1 and R4 classes, 29 sites).
- To route C or way 5, the team's clause: the self-typed traits of the library carry `comprises X`, under which the idiom of `var-ref.tex:64-69` types `self` and rule (a) is not reached; that needs the clause on the seven traits, walk's row 407 repaired first, and leave in `traits.tex` for a static parameter as a listed type, which Welterweight's grammar does not admit (the judgement, section 3, "Way 5"). The entry's Route C item says so.

## 4. What it bends

The record's reading of route A, "no self type enters the library" (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-8.md:113`), is set aside by P-146 itself: the library's text gains no self type and no clause, but the checker gives `self` a self type in every trait with a self-type parameter, the library's among them. Route A (P-43) and the `comprises` decision (P-44) stand: under a `comprises` clause the self type is the clause's, and rule (a) is never reached there.

content.content:
## 1. The question, in plain words

Terms first.

- A **self-typed trait** is a generic trait whose type parameter stands for the implementing type itself: `trait Integral[\I extends Integral[\I\]\]` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:680`). Each integer type implements it at itself, `trait ZZ32 extends { AnyIntegral, Integral[\ZZ32\] }` (`:724`). The bound `I extends Integral[\I\]` is an **F-bound**: the parameter's bound names the parameter.
- Inside such a trait, the specification types `self` as the trait's own type, `Integral[\I\]` (`Specification/basic/expressions/var-ref.tex:53-54`). Nothing in that rule says that `self` is an `I`.
- A **self type** is a further fact a language may give `self`: that it is also an `I`. Scala declares it (`this: S =>`), Rust builds it in (`Self`), the Fortress team's compiled-world idiom declares it with `comprises I`, and under it the checker types `self` as the intersection `Integral[\I\] & I` (`var-ref.tex:63-69`; `SelfParamDisambiguator.scala:56-75`; `TypeAnalyzer.removeSelf`, `:488-501`).

The error. 30 of the last landed distance's 153 are bodies of self-typed traits that return `self` where `I` is declared, pass `self` where an `I` is expected, or convert `self` into `ZZ` (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-12/gate/distance.txt:21-22`: S1 29, R4 1). The message is "Function body has type Integral[\I\], but declared return type is I." (`compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv:109-114`). Walk runs every one of them, since it has no static types. The ways note's section 1 lists the sites: by trait, the orders 16, `AdditiveGroup` 2, `Integral` 8, `StandardMutableArrayType` 4; by shape, A (`self` passed, 11 errors plus 5 cascades), B (`self` returned, 13), C (`self` converted into `ZZ`, 1, at `:685`). I take that list as the sites and do not re-gather it.

The question for him: which way makes the 30 check without changing what walk computes.

....
### Way 6: the self type read from the F-bound, checked at each extender

- What. Two rules, no new syntax.
  - (a) In a trait declaration `C[\X_1, ..., X_n\]`, a type parameter `X_k` whose `extends` clause lists `C[\X_1, ..., X_n\]`, the trait at its own parameters, is the trait's self parameter, and the type of `self` in the trait's methods is `C[\X_1, ..., X_n\] ∩ X_k`. This is the type the checker already gives `self` under `comprises X_k` (`SelfParamDisambiguator.scala:63-75`; `TypeAnalyzer.removeSelf`), read from the bound instead of a clause.
  - (b) A trait or object declaration, or an object expression, that extends an instantiation `C[\A_1, ..., A_n\]` of such a trait must have a self type that is a subtype of `A_k`, where a declaration's self type is its own type, or `D[\...\] ∩ Y` when the declaration has a self parameter `Y` by (a). A declaration that fails this is a static error. This is Scala's conformance rule, and it is what makes (a) sound: `object Bad extends Integral[\ZZ32\]` is refused, so inside `Integral[\I\]` every `self` is an `I`. Checking direct extensions at every declaration suffices, by induction up the hierarchy: a value of `C[\A\]` comes from an object whose every supertrait was checked.
- What it changes. The checker: the self type at `SelfParamDisambiguator.scala:63-75` (about 15 lines), and the extender check beside the `comprises` checks in `TypeHierarchyChecker.checkDeclComprises`'s loop over `extendsTypes` (`:208-258`, about 25 lines), with object expressions wherever their self type is formed (`getObjectExprType`). The specification: one sentence at `var-ref.tex:63-69` beside the idiom, the extender rule in the traits chapter, an Appendix I entry. The library: nothing. Walk: nothing, since walk does no static typing and no clause reaches its exclusion test, so row 407 does not arise.
- What stays the same, by reading of the checker. Everything but the typing of `self` in bodies. The overloading check strips a self type to its trait (`OverloadingOracle.scala:368`, `:380`, `:411-414`); so do the overload sets (`OverloadSet.java:793-795`), the exclusion oracle (`ExclusionOracle.scala:148-150`), the coercion oracle (`CoercionOracle.scala:176`), the variance checker (`VarianceChecker.scala:214-220`) and the code generator (`CodeGen.java:3672-3674`). `Integral[\ZZ32\]` stays a type of its own, not identified with `ZZ32`: no subtyping, exclusion or hierarchy verdict between trait types moves, which is why the route C overflow's cause (the clause's effect on `comprisesClause` under an exclusion question) is not reached. The intersection flows only where `self` flows: into subtyping, where `Integral[\I\] & I <: I` holds at once (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:163`), and into the exclusion test of an argument type (`pExcInner`, `:409`), which is the one path unmeasured (below).
- Clears. 29 by reading: every shape A and B site, the 5 cascades and R4's tuple with them. Every library extender passes (b): the five integer types, `RR64`, `RR32`, `QQ`, `String`, `Char`, `Boolean`, `CaseInsensitiveString`, `Range[\I\]`, `Vector`, `Matrix`, `Array1-3` extend at themselves (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:293`, `:391`, `:482-639`, `:1603`, `:1721`, `:1577-1796`, `:2163`, `:2419`; `FortressBuiltin.fsi:47`, `:131`, `:225-228`; `CaseInsensitiveString.fsi:21`); `Comparison` at itself and `TotalComparison` below it (`.fsi:101`, `:120-121`); `Integral[\I\]`, `MultiplicativeRing[\T\]` and `LexicographicOrder[\T,E\]` pass through their own self types (`:275`, `:443`, `:1334`); the test and model types extend at themselves too (`tests/parametricManiaCompr.fss:20`, `demos/trips.fss:51`, `library_tests/MaybeTest9.fss:19`, `EqualityRung1.fss:19`; C4's `Diag` is a `Matrix[\RR64,s,s\]`, `run-c4/src/FlatArrays.fss:36`). This is the distance stage's class S1, 28 errors.

- Haskell's class defaults are typed at the instance, so the Prelude's `max x y` returns `x :: a` (Haskell 2010 Report, chapter 6, the `Ord` class; not fetched).
     - Under any of these the library's bodies check as written.
   - **An F-bound, `this` typed as the trait.**
     - Java uses `(T) this` or the "getThis" trick (FAQ206 above).
     - Scala declares a self type: "Inside the template, the type of `this` is assumed to be S"; "The self type of a class or object must conform to the self types of all classes which are inherited by the template" (*Scala Language Specification 2.13*, §5.1, Templates, https://www.scala-lang.org/files/archive/spec/2.13/05-classes-and-objects.html).
     - C#'s `INumber<TSelf>` declares its operators as static members over `TSelf` (literature note `:56`), which is way 7's shape.
     - Cecil, C#, Swift and Scala flatten the algebra (literature note §6).
